sentences.text: Kangnasaurus was a bipedal herbivore related to early iguanodontians.
Sidney H. Haughton named the genus in 1915 after Kangnas farm, while the species name honors farmer Coetzee.
The defining specimen is a single tooth recovered from a well at Farm Kangnas in the Orange River valley of South Africa.
Haughton also described other fossils, such as partial thigh bones, shin bones, and vertebrae, that he thought belonged to the animal.
Recent research places Kangnasaurus within the elasmarian group.
Sedimentological analyses suggest the animal lived during the Late Cretaceous, between the Campanian and Maastrichtian periods.
However, some sources propose an earlier age at the start of the Cretaceous, while the Paleobiology Database lists a range from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian.

It is debated whether additional fossils described by Sidney H. Haughton and a researcher named Cooper actually belong to Kangnasaurus, as some of those bones may have originated from geological deposits other than the one where the defining tooth was found.
